name: States of matter and changes of state

questions.q: Which of the following describes the particle arrangement and motion in a solid?
a: Regularly arranged, vibrating about fixed positions
Randomly arranged, moving rapidly in all directions
Far apart, sliding past each other slowly
Closely packed, moving freely throughout the container

Which of the following physical changes is exothermic?
Why are gases easily compressible compared to solids and liquids?
a: Because there are large empty spaces between gas particles
Because gas particles are soft and squishy
Because gas particles shrink under external pressure
Because liquids lack any intermolecular forces

questions.q: What name is given to the random motion of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid, caused by collisions with fast-moving molecules?
When a bottle of perfume is opened, its scent spreads across the room. What process causes this?
Which factor increases the rate of diffusion of a gas?
a: Increasing the molecular mass of the gas particles

questions.q: Gas A has a relative molecular mass Mr of 16, and Gas B has a relative molecular mass Mr of 64. Which gas will diffuse faster at room temperature?
a: Gas A, because it has a lower molecular mass and its particles travel faster
Gas B, because it is heavier and carries more momentum
Both will diffuse at exactly the same speed
Gas B, because heavier particles move quicker

questions.q: What happens to the average kinetic energy of water molecules when water is heated from 20 °C to 80 °C?
Which state of matter has a fixed volume but no fixed shape?
What is the term for the phase change from a gas to a liquid?

a: Closer to the hydrogen chloride end, because HCl has a higher relative molecular mass and diffuses slower
Closer to the ammonia end, because it is heavier
In the exact middle of the tube

questions.q: How does evaporation differ from boiling?
a: Evaporation occurs only at the boiling point throughout the liquid
Evaporation occurs only at the surface and at any temperature below the boiling point
Boiling does not require energy input
Evaporation requires an external flame source

questions.q: Which statement best describes the forces of attraction between particles in an ideal gas?
a: Very strong forces holding them in a rigid lattice
Moderate forces allowing them to slide past each other
Negligible or zero forces of attraction under normal conditions

questions.q: What occurs physically at the melting point of a pure substance?
a: Gas bubbles form throughout the solid
The solid turns directly into a vapor
Particles gain enough energy to break out of their fixed positions in the lattice, forming a liquid

questions.q: If solid iodine is heated gently and turns directly into purple vapor without melting, what is this process called?
Why does a puddle of water evaporate faster on a warm, windy day than on a cold, calm day?
a: Wind decreases humidity and warmth slows down particles
Higher temperature increases particle kinetic energy and wind removes vapor molecules, increasing the rate of evaporation
The water undergoes chemical reactions with the wind
Cold air causes the water to sublime

questions.q: Which substance sublimes rather than melts under normal atmospheric pressure?

Which graph feature represents a pure substance changing from a liquid to a solid during a cooling curve?
a: A flat horizontal section (plateau) where temperature remains constant while changing state
A straight vertical line pointing upwards
A continuous downward slope with no flat sections
A horizontal line at zero pressure

questions.q: What happens to the average distance between particles when a substance freezes into a solid?
a: Distance generally decreases as particles settle into a structured, close-packed lattice
Distance remains identical to the gas phase

questions.q: Which property distinguishes a liquid from a gas?
a: Liquids have particles held close together by attractive forces, limiting volume changes

questions.q: What causes pressure inside a sealed container filled with gas?
a: Collisions of fast-moving gas particles with the interior walls of the container

questions.q: Comparing the diffusion of sulfur dioxide (SO<sub>2</sub>, Mr = 64) and methane (CH<sub>4</sub>, Mr = 16), which diffuses faster and by what factor?
a: Methane diffuses twice as fast as sulfur dioxide
Sulfur dioxide diffuses four times faster than methane

questions.q: Which phase change involves particles losing thermal energy to the surroundings?
A student heats a solid crystal until it melts and then boils. Which sequence shows increasing disorder (entropy) of the particles?
Why does a closed metal container filled with air increase in internal pressure when heated?
a: The number of gas molecules increases
The volume of individual gas molecules expands
Particles gain kinetic energy, colliding more frequently and with greater force against the walls

questions.q: What term describes the conversion of a liquid into a gas at any temperature below its boiling point?
What happens to the temperature of boiling water as it continues to boil vigorously in an open beaker?
a: It remains constant at its boiling point

questions.q: Which of the following provides direct evidence for the particulate nature of matter via random particle motion?
a: Brownian motion of smoke particles suspended in air

questions.q: If the temperature of an ideal gas in a rigid container is doubled on the Kelvin scale, what happens to the average speed of its particles?
a: It increases, as higher temperature corresponds to higher average kinetic energy

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares solid and gas states?
a: Solid particles vibrate about fixed positions; gas particles move randomly at high speeds
Solid particles are far apart; gas particles are tightly bound
Solids can flow easily; gases maintain rigid shapes

questions.q: What term describes a substance that has melted into a liquid state?
During a phase change from liquid to gas, thermal energy supplied is used primarily for what purpose?
a: To increase the speed of individual molecules within the gas
To overcome the forces of attraction holding particles together in the liquid state
To increase the mass of individual molecules

questions.q: Which of the following gases diffuses the slowest in air at room temperature?
What is the physical state of bromine (Br<sub>2</sub>) at 25 °C, given its melting point is -7 °C and boiling point is 59 °C?
Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker than in an open saucepan?
a: Food is stirred automatically by steam
Increased pressure inside the cooker raises the boiling point of water, allowing cooking at higher temperatures
Pressure lowers the kinetic energy of water molecules
Cooling occurs faster under high pressure

questions.q: Which phenomenon provides visual evidence of random particle motion in liquids?
a: Pollen grains moving randomly when viewed under a microscope in water

questions.q: What happens to the density of most substances when they change from a liquid to a solid?
a: Density generally increases because particles pack more closely together
